37-#### Context
38-
39-The harness keeps its context between requests instead of starting fresh each time. Tasks share one ongoing conversation, and each task sent carries it on. When the project is opened, tasks carry on the latest conversation in its history. Questions from the Ask tab share a separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is in the background, and if one can't be carried on, the next request starts a new one. Each run applies its own prompt's systemPrompt, even when it carries on a conversation begun in a different mode. The palette's file search always starts fresh.
40-A conversation can be left for a new one, from the chat input's New conversation button, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says: the next request starts a new conversation with no context, and the one left is not carried on again, not by a run of it still going, nor by the project's history. Leaving it is kept with the project, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, so a project opened after its tasks' or questions' conversation was left starts a new one too, rather than carrying on the latest conversation in its history, until a run after the reset begins one of its own. How much context a conversation holds is known from what the harness reports with each reply: everything the model was given, cached or not, and what it wrote, as of its latest reply; replies of subagents don't count.

Its row counts every task but the latest, which heads the view: "No previous tasks", "1 previous task", or "N previous tasks", and each offers Resend. Until it has compiled, the prompt as typed is shown instead. At its right, a Resend button sends it again, as the [PromptSendingScope](./sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says. 41-#### Queue
42-
43-```
44-overview: The queue holds the tasks sent while the harness is working, as the [PromptSendingScope](./sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says, in the order they were sent, and sends them one at a time.
45-placement: The queue sits along the bottom of the view, below the output and directly above the chat input, with a border along its top. It is not part of the header. A row saying how many prompts are queued, with a chevron, expands to list each queued prompt in order, a line or two of each, with a button to cancel it. Each prompt in the list is numbered, with its number, text, and cancel button vertically centred in its row, and the list scrolls once it gets tall, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope). Each time it is expanded, it opens scrolled to the bottom, on the prompts queued most recently, however it was scrolled when last closed. The same area holds the auto-send switch and the "Send next" button. The queue is shown only while it has anything in it.
46-cancel: A queued prompt that has not been sent yet can be cancelled, which removes it from the queue for good. A prompt already sent is no longer in the queue.
47-editing: Each queued prompt in the list also has a button with a pencil icon, before its cancel button, whose tooltip says it edits the prompt. Clicking it edits the prompt in the [ChatInputScope](./chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), as it says, and its row is highlighted while it is being edited. While it is, it is held where it is: it is never sent, and a queue waiting on it waits, even with auto-send on. Saving the edit puts the new text, in the mode and with the attachments it was saved with, in its place in the queue, saved with the project in place of what it held, then lets the queue go on as before. An edit that can't be saved leaves the prompt as it was, and a notification titled "Could not save the queued prompt" says why. Cancelling the edit, or cancelling the prompt from the list meanwhile, leaves the queue as it was, less that prompt when it was cancelled.

49-autoSend: A "Send next automatically" switch picks between sending the next queued prompt as soon as the harness is free, and waiting. It starts switched on. Switching it on while the harness is free sends the next queued prompt straight away. Whenever the harness is free and the queue is not empty, a "Send next" button sends the first queued prompt.

The queue is restored the first time the project is opened in a launch; a restored queue waits for "Send next" rather than sending on its own. A queued prompt's file is removed when it is cancelled, or when it is sent, at which point it is saved to the prompt history like any other prompt.
